title: Engineering
summary: How the app is built where that has to hold.
description: Rules that hold across the whole code base.

requirements.text: The frontend is React and TypeScript in a Tauri 2 shell; SQLite runs in Rust and the frontend queries it through drizzle.

deprecation.reason: Engineering rules are specified by the shared part Keel, imported into this spec, whose requirement promises the same.

requirements.text: `bun run build` typechecks `src/`, lints everything and bundles, and fails on any type or lint error.

deprecation.reason: Engineering rules are specified by the shared part Keel, imported into this spec, whose requirement promises the same.

requirements.text: `bun test` checks the spec: schema, unique ids, references, histories, that every imported part is unchanged from where it was copied, and that every `Spec:` citation in the code names a requirement that holds here, not a waived one.

history.text: `bun test` checks the spec: schema, unique ids, references, histories, and that every `Spec:` citation in the code names a requirement.
history.reason: The spec imports shared parts: a copy that was edited, or code citing a requirement the product waived, is caught too.

requirements.text: CI runs `bun test` and `bun run build` on every push.
On every push to main, CI builds the app for every platform in `app.platforms` and publishes the builds to the `latest` release.
Frontend packages are installed only once they have been published for `deps.minimum-age`.

requirements.text: The macOS app is signed (ad hoc while there's no certificate), so macOS asks before letting it onto the local network instead of keeping it off without asking.
